rubric_items.reason: All nine design components (patientsRouter through AppointmentDetailPage) have at least one threat. The three endpoints are covered through their components.

Most threats fit the change (medical history leaking into list items, SQL injection through search, an N+1 lookup, XSS through doctor_name). T-7 is a strawman because the design leaves AppointmentRepo untouched, and T-11 assumes settings get extended.

Most new controls are concrete and testable (explicit field list plus a test, bound parameters, no wildcard select, plain-text rendering). T-1 and T-2 call identify/requirePermission controls even though the MVP grants everything.
Assumptions T-4, T-8 and T-10 are stated, each with a basis. Deployment reachability is asked as Q-01. The assumptions are handed to the implement step rather than asked as questions.
Readable and consistent between the front matter and the body. Threats are listed in component order, not by risk.

findings.text: T-1 and T-2 present identify and requirePermission as existing controls, but the cited architecture says that in the MVP every permission is granted. These calls give no protection today.

cites.quote: Existing control: the route keeps its current requirePermission check (C2).
In the MVP every request is the actor `staff` and every permission is granted.

findings.suggested_fix: State plainly that in the MVP there is no effective access control on GET /api/patients, and that the only real mitigation is the deployment boundary asked in Q-01.

findings.text: T-11 describes extending settings to carry the time zone. The design says useSettings and GET /api/settings are existing and unchanged, and already supply the zone. The threat does not match the design.

cites.quote: Extending settings to carry the time zone exposes other configuration through GET /api/settings.
GET /api/settings — existing: unchanged; source of the hospital time zone for the web app.

findings.suggested_fix: Either reframe T-11 around a threat to the unchanged route, or ask whether settings already carry the zone.

findings.text: T-7 is a strawman. It assumes the ticket changes appointment code paths, which the design rules out, so the threat adds no protection.

cites.quote: The ticket changes appointment code paths and so weakens how appointments are written.
AppointmentRepo (module:sample-system:api) — existing: not used for this lookup.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace T-7 with a threat specific to AppointmentRepo's role here, or note that it is out of scope and give the reason.

findings.text: No threat covers what the new column itself reveals. Each patient's next doctor appears on the list, and doctors have specializations, so the list can imply a patient's condition even with medical history excluded.

cites.quote: The widened list gives every caller the next appointment of every patient
A doctor has one specialization, one department

findings.suggested_fix: Add an information_disclosure threat for this inference risk, and a product question on whether showing the doctor on the list is acceptable.

findings.text: Threats are listed in component order rather than by risk. The highest-risk items (T-1, T-3, T-6) are not grouped first.

cites.quote: T-1 (patientsRouter, spoofing): non-staff caller treated as staff in the MVP

findings.suggested_fix: Order the Threats section by risk, or add a risk rating to each threat.
